metaDescription: Soundbars under $300 compared by channels, subwoofer type, Dolby Atmos claims, dialogue modes and TV remote control, with honest notes on virtual surround.
expertTake: The Samsung HW-B630F is the best overall pick because it adds a dedicated centre channel and TV remote control to a 3.1 layout with a subwoofer. The TCL S55H is the best value for Dolby Atmos support with auto room calibration. Skip Atmos-branded soundbars at this cap if you expect sound from the ceiling, because virtual height from a bar in front of you is an effect, not a second room of speakers.
introParagraphs: A soundbar is the simplest upgrade for a living room whose television speakers sound thin, and the useful upgrade at this cap is a separate subwoofer and a dedicated dialogue channel. The numbers on the box, channels and watts, describe configuration and peak output, and they say less about how voices and bass will sound in your room.

The cap reflects listing prices on the day we updated the guide, and prices move often. We kept this lineup distinct from our lower cap soundbar guides by looking at bars that add a subwoofer, a centre channel or a stated format. We have not handled any of these soundbars, so our judgments rest on specifications and patterns in owner feedback, including how virtual surround and wireless subwoofers behave in real rooms.

products.name: Samsung B-Series HW-B630F 3.1 Channel Soundbar with Subwoofer, DTS Virtual:X, TV remote control
products.description:
This is a 3.1 channel soundbar with a subwoofer, and its distinguishing feature is a dedicated centre channel speaker that the listing says makes voices extra clear. DTS Virtual:X creates a wider soundstage from the bar's front-facing speakers, and the bar responds to a Samsung TV remote for power, volume and source. The 3.1 layout is the right configuration for dialogue-heavy viewing.

The tradeoff is that virtual surround is processed, not physical, and the effect varies with room shape and seating position. Compared with the 2.1 B550F, the B630F adds the centre channel, and the extra clarity for speech is the reason to pay for it. Wireless subwoofers need a power outlet and a spot within range, which can limit where you put it.

Place the bar directly in front of the TV at ear height or just below it, and keep the subwoofer a few inches from a wall for a tighter sound. Check that your TV has an ARC or eARC HDMI port. Update the firmware and adjust the dialogue and bass levels to your room.
products.bestFor: A living room where clear dialogue matters more than a big surround effect.
pros: Dedicated centre channel is listed for clearer voices
Wireless subwoofer adds real bass over a 2.0 bar
Works with a Samsung TV remote for basic control
DTS Virtual:X widens the soundstage from a single bar
cons: Virtual surround varies with room and seating
Wireless subwoofer needs an outlet and a sensible spot

products.name: TCL S55H 2.1 Sound Bar with Wireless Subwoofer, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, auto room calibration, 220 W
products.description:
This bar combines a 2.1 layout and a wireless subwoofer with support for Dolby Atmos and DTS:X formats, plus an automatic room calibration feature that adjusts output to your space. The maker lists up to 220 watts of power. Format support means the bar accepts the signals streaming apps send, and the calibration is a handy feature in a room with odd acoustics.

The compromise is that a 2.1 bar with Atmos support does not have height speakers, so the ceiling effect is virtual, and the compact data does not list a centre channel. Compared with the Samsung B630F, it is less dialogue-focused but adds format support and calibration. Auto calibration helps but cannot fix a bar placed in a cabinet.

Run the calibration with the room at its normal level of furniture and curtains. Place the subwoofer where the sound is even. Set the dialogue mode if voices sound buried.
products.bestFor: A budget-friendly way to get Atmos-compatible sound and room calibration.

products.name: ULTIMEA Poseidon M60 5.1 Channel Soundbar with Dolby Atmos, 300 W, wired subwoofer, VoiceMX
products.description:
This is a 5.1 channel system with five built-in full-range drivers and a dedicated wired subwoofer, rated at 300 watts, with Dolby Atmos and a voice clarity feature the maker calls VoiceMX. The listing describes a wooden subwoofer cabinet, which usually gives tighter bass than plastic. A 5.1 layout from a single bar is a bold claim at this cap.

The tradeoff is that a wired subwoofer limits placement, and the bar's surround channels are virtual, since five drivers in one bar cannot sit behind you. Compared with the Hiwill, which has two front surround speakers, the ULTIMEA is more standard. Brand reputation is thinner than JBL or Samsung, so check the warranty.

Run the subwoofer cable neatly and keep it out of walkways. Test the app control during the return window. Use the voice mode for dialogue-heavy shows.
products.bestFor: A shopper who wants the longest channel and feature list for the cost.

Wooden subwoofer cabinet is described

products.name: JBL Bar 2.1 Deep Bass MK2 with Wireless 6.5 inch Subwoofer, 300 W max, Bluetooth
products.description:
This bar pairs a 2.1 channel soundbar with a wireless 6.5 inch subwoofer, quoting 300 watts of maximum system output and JBL's surround sound processing, plus Bluetooth for music. It is the best-known brand in the group and the one most likely to have clear support documentation. The 6.5 inch sub gives a meaningful bass boost over a bar-only system.

The tradeoff is that 300 watts is a peak figure, and a 2.1 bar has no centre channel, so dialogue clarity depends on processing. Compared with the Samsung B630F, the JBL has no TV-remote integration listed but offers a stronger bass driver. Maximum output is not a measure of how loud it plays cleanly.

Place the subwoofer where bass is even and not in a corner, which can make it boomy. Set the bar to the TV's ARC input. Use the movie and voice modes to taste.

products.name: Hiwill 4.1 Channel Sound Bar with Dolby Atmos, 300 W, subwoofer, 2 front surround speakers
products.description:
This is a 4.1 channel bar with a subwoofer and two front surround speakers, with four aluminium-magnesium alloy diaphragm drivers and 300 watts quoted. The listing positions it against thin mini soundbars, promising a wider soundstage and spatial audio from Dolby Atmos. Two surround speakers placed at the sides of the bar give a more natural sense of width.

The compromise is that front surround speakers sit in front of you, so they widen the sound without wrapping behind you. Compared with the ULTIMEA, the Hiwill's detachable surrounds are a different approach, and the brand is similarly less established. Check the listing for subwoofer connection type.

Place the surround speakers a few feet to each side of the bar, angled slightly in. Adjust their level in the app or remote. Test the Atmos setting with a known demo scene.

products.name: Samsung B-Series HW-B550F 2.1 Channel Soundbar with Subwoofer, DTS Virtual:X, Voice Enhance, Bass Boost
products.description:
This is a 2.1 channel Samsung with a subwoofer, DTS Virtual:X, a Voice Enhance mode and an extra bass setting. It is a simpler cousin of the B630F without the dedicated centre channel, and it covers the basics: a bar, a sub and dialogue help. The voice mode lifts speech over the soundtrack.

The tradeoff is that a 2.1 layout has to fake a centre channel, so a dedicated centre, as on the B630F, is clearer for dialogue. Compared with the TCL, it has fewer format claims but easier TV integration. A bass boost mode can make the subwoofer boomy in a small room.

Use the voice mode for dialogue and turn the bass boost down if neighbours complain. Keep the sub away from corners. Update the firmware when prompted.

products.name: Polk Audio Signa S2 Ultra-Slim Sound Bar with Wireless Subwoofer, VoiceAdjust, 5 full-range drivers
products.description:
This bar is just over 2 inches tall, so it sits under most TVs without blocking the screen or the remote sensor, and it has five full-range drivers and a wireless subwoofer. VoiceAdjust technology lets you raise dialogue over the soundtrack. The listing says it sounds on par with mid- to high-range bars at its size.

The tradeoff is that an ultra-slim bar has small drivers and little internal space, so bass relies on the subwoofer. Compared with the JBL, the Polk is slimmer and has a stronger dialogue feature, but fewer format claims. It also appears in our lower cap soundbar guide.

Place it on a shelf where it is not blocked, and set VoiceAdjust to a level that suits your hearing. Keep the subwoofer away from the TV to avoid vibration.

buyingCriteria.explanation: At this cap you can buy a separate subwoofer, a centre channel, a stated format and sometimes TV remote integration. The Samsung B630F adds a centre channel, the TCL adds auto calibration, and the ULTIMEA and Hiwill add channel counts. The lower cap bars skip the subwoofer or the format. Measure the width of your TV and the space on the stand, because a bar should be about as wide as the TV or slightly narrower, and a very wide bar looks and sounds awkward under a small screen.

A 2.1 bar has left, right and a subwoofer, and a 3.1 bar adds a dedicated centre for dialogue. A 5.1 bar in one chassis still simulates its rear channels. For speech clarity, a centre channel helps more than extra watts. If you rent or move often, favour wireless subwoofers over wired ones, since a cable run across the floor is a nuisance in a new layout.

A wireless subwoofer is easier to place, but it needs an outlet and sometimes pairing. A wired sub, as on the ULTIMEA, limits placement but avoids pairing problems. A built-in sub in a thin bar is weaker.

Dolby Atmos support means the bar accepts the signal, and without up-firing speakers the height effect is virtual. DTS Virtual:X is a processing mode. Treat both as helpful effects and not true surround.
HDMI ARC lets one cable carry audio to the bar and lets your TV remote control volume. An optical input works but may limit formats. Check your TV's ports before buying.
A bar should sit under the TV without blocking the screen or the remote sensor. A bar over 3 inches tall can block a low TV. The Polk is just over 2 inches high.

specDecoder.meaning: The number of separate audio channels, such as 2.1 or 3.1. The .1 is the subwoofer. A 3.1 layout dedicates a speaker to the middle of the soundstage, which is where most speech sits.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Samsung B630F is 3.1, TCL and JBL 2.1, Hiwill 4.1 and ULTIMEA 5.1.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum power output claimed. It is not a measure of clean volume. Peak output is the burst a system can manage for a moment, and sustained output is usually well below it.
specDecoder.watchFor: The JBL, ULTIMEA and Hiwill quote 300 W and the TCL 220 W.

specDecoder.meaning: A processing mode that simulates a wider and taller sound from a bar. Virtual surround works best when you sit in the middle of the room, and the effect narrows off to the sides.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Samsung bars and TCL list DTS Virtual:X or DTS:X.

specDecoder.meaning: A format with height information. Without up-firing speakers, a bar renders it virtually. Because the signal is processed, an Atmos bar may need the TV set to bitstream or pass-through to receive the format.
specDecoder.watchFor: The TCL, ULTIMEA and Hiwill list Atmos.

specDecoder.meaning: A feature that measures your room and adjusts output. Calibration microphones sit in the bar or the remote, so avoid blocking them during the test tones.
specDecoder.watchFor: The TCL lists auto room calibration.

howWeEvaluated.title: Configuration and channels
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each bar on the channel layout and speakers stated in its listing. The Samsung B630F's centre channel and the ULTIMEA's 5.1 layout lead. We have not handled any of these bars.

howWeEvaluated.title: Subwoofer and bass
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared subwoofer type and size. The JBL lists a 6.5 inch wireless sub, and the ULTIMEA lists a wired wooden sub. Owner feedback patterns often mention boomy or absent bass.

howWeEvaluated.title: Formats and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered Atmos, DTS and calibration. We say plainly that virtual height is an effect. We do not publish ratings or review counts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Distinct from lower caps
howWeEvaluated.description: We avoided repeating our lower cap lineups, with one carry-over, the Polk. We left out wall mounts, PC speakers and non-soundbar items.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: Peak watts and channel counts are marketing numbers, and we say so.

cards.label: 2.1 or 3.1, like Samsung
cards.text: Simpler and neater. A centre channel helps dialogue, and virtual surround is subtle.

cards.label: 5.1 in a bar, like ULTIMEA
cards.text: More channels on paper. The rears are simulated, and the sub is wired.

howToChoose.note: Choose 3.1 for dialogue and 5.1 for a bigger spec sheet.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A subwoofer, a centre channel or voice mode, HDMI ARC and a bar that fits under your TV.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Samsung B630F is the best all-round pick, and the TCL is the best value.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want true up-firing Atmos speakers, wireless rear speakers, Wi-Fi streaming or room correction that works well.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You mainly want clearer dialogue and some bass. A 2.1 bar with a sub is enough.

faq.a: For real bass, yes. A subwoofer makes a noticeable difference to movies and music. Turn on night mode if you watch late, because it compresses loud scenes and reduces bass.

faq.q: What does Dolby Atmos mean on a soundbar?
faq.a: It means the bar accepts Atmos signals, and without up-firing speakers the height effect is virtual.
Not much. They are marketing numbers, and clean volume is more important.

faq.q: Where should I put the subwoofer?
faq.a: On the floor near the front of the room, a few inches from a wall, and not in a corner.
